newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends unchanged, downside risk limited.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends unchanged, downside risk limited.

text.p: Key December Euroyen futures contract on TIFFE ended Monday's day session unchanged, but its downside was getting hard to crack after expectations for an early credit tightening faded away, traders said.

"Since last Wednesday's "tankan", (Bank of Japan's key corporate survey) more and more traders have come to a conclusion that there would be no rate hike by the end of this year," said a Japanese city bank trader.
With the slow pace of recovery confirmed by the tankan, traders started to focus on a possible supplementary budget which may be adopted in the coming few months.
It would theoretically put upward pressure on the longer end of the yield curve due to bond issues to finance it.

"But the state budget balance is such bad shape to have a giant size supplementary budget, so even if it were adopted, it is unlikely to have a big negative impact on the overall debt market," said another city bank trader.
Meanwhile, the BOJ maintained its neutral stance, leaving the market with a small 10 billion yen shortfall.
The key three-month certificate of deposit was at a sell quotation of 0.53 percent, down from 0.54 percent on Friday.
Some traders said that opinions are divided over if the BOJ will be able to tighten its grip by next March when the current fiscal year ends.
"They (the BOJ) have missed the chance (of tightening) in May and in July, so they might as well miss it again during the current fiscal year," said a brokerage trader.
The key overnight call rate was traded at 0.47-0.48 percent, mostly unchanged from Friday's weighted average of 0.47 percent. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk 813-3432-8676
